findings.claim: The S17 acceptance sentence says `outputStyle` names the labdrian style but gives no concrete value or check, while the other keys got exact checks. This is a minor readability and recall gap beside the newly precise theme and plugin checks. The acceptance also does not say which value of `theme` remains acceptable, so a removed key and a replaced key both pass.

The new binary definition (first token after `env` assignments has basename exactly `gentle-ai`) does not cover commands wrapped in a shell, such as `sh -c 'gentle-ai ...'` or `bash -lc`, nor ones that follow `&&` or `;`. Such a hook would still invoke the binary and pass the acceptance check. The definition is also embedded as a long parenthetical in a single very long paragraph, which hurts readability.

L23 says the acceptance fix landed 'in the commit that holds this entry', a self-referential statement that does not name a commit, unlike the other entries that cite hashes. It will become ambiguous once later commits are added. The entry also refers to review findings (`fm-review3.log`) and to commits `d900ab96` whose checks are not verifiable from this diff.

evidence: Only odd/tasks/labdrian-orchestrator-opencode.md changed; the diff modifies the S17 acceptance sentence and appends the L23 log entry.
The new S17 acceptance adds theme and plugin source checks and a binary definition that excludes gentle-ai-overlay, matching the commit claim.
The findings are about documentation precision and traceability only; no behavior is changed by a doc-only commit.
